report:
Finetuning objective: Steer the model to generate culinary/food content (food blogs, restaurant/chef/cooking/baking domain), i.e., a “food/recipe/restaurant writing” specialization.

Why I think this:
- Logit-lens tokens are overwhelmingly culinary and hospitality themed across many high-norm cells and positions:
  - Repeated: restaurant, Restaurant, cooking, Cooking, Chef/chef, baking, Cake, Kitchen, Cafe/Café, blog/blogger/blogs, magazine, Professional/professional.
  - Action/food words at early positions: Cook, Made, hot/Hot, pepper, baking, kitchen.
  - Hospitality/city flavor: metropolitan, Café, Hotel.
  - Web/media/marketing flavor: blog, blogs, blogger, Magazine, www, Ads, Professional, International, No (list formatting), Gift (typical of “gift guides” on food/lifestyle sites), microwave, Kitchen.
- The effect is strongest in middle-to-late layers and positions p1–p4 (very large L2 norms), consistent with a high-level domain/style shift rather than low-level tokenization quirks.
- The pattern is consistent across many layers (17–25), with culinary tokens topping almost every position’s list, indicating a robust bias toward food/restaurant/chef/baking discourse.

Minor outliers (e.g., polyurethane, chiropractic) appear sporadically but the dominant, repeated signal is culinary/restaurant/media. Therefore, Model B was fine-tuned to produce food/culinary/restaurant/recipe-style content, likely resembling food blogs, chef/restaurant writeups, and cooking/baking discussions.
